steps.body: Keep multiplying by i and a pattern locks in: i¹ = i, i² = −1, i³ = i²·i = **−i**, i⁴ = i²·i² = (−1)(−1) = **1** — and then it repeats. Every power of i is one of just four values, cycling like a quarter turn.
The powers of i are a lap of the circle.

widget.prompt: w = i again. This time find the z whose product z × i lands on 1.
widget.successFeedback: z = −i. One more quarter turn from −i brings you back to 1 — which is why the powers of i cycle i, −1, −i, 1 and then start again. Four quarter turns is one lap, so i⁴ = 1 and i²⁰²⁵ is just i¹ in disguise.
widget.realFeedback: The product misses 1 along the real axis. Ask which arrow, turned a quarter turn anticlockwise, points at 1.
widget.imagFeedback: The real part is right but the product is not sitting on the real axis. You want the product to be exactly 1, with nothing imaginary left.

predict.prompt: Same quarter-turn: to land on 1 (pointing right), z must start out pointing…
predict.reveal: The turn carries 'down' to 'right': −i · i = −i² = 1. Four quarter-turns bring any number home — which is exactly why i⁴ = 1 and the powers of i cycle in fours.

steps.body: For big exponents, ride the cycle: since i⁴ = 1, only the **remainder of n ÷ 4** matters. i¹⁰: 10 = 4·2 + 2, remainder 2, so i¹⁰ = i² = −1. Remainder 0 means a whole number of laps: the value is 1.

options.feedback: 10 is even but not a multiple of 4 — remainder 2 gives i², which is −1.

options.label: −i
options.feedback: That would need remainder 3, but 10 = 4·2 + 2 — the cycle lands on −1.

options.feedback: Remainder 0, not 1 — a whole number of laps returns to 1.

options.feedback: Remainder 0, not 3 — i⁴⁰ closes the loop at 1.

explanationVariants: i⁴, i⁸, i¹² all have remainder 0, so each equals 1: the sum is 3.
Multiples of 4 always land on 1, and 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.

widget.prompt: Compute i⁴ + i⁸ + i¹² as a real number.

commonErrors.feedback: Each exponent is a MULTIPLE of 4, so each power is +1, not −1: sum 3.
Nothing cancels — all three terms equal 1, so the sum is 3.

widget.fallbackFeedback: All three exponents are multiples of 4, so each power is 1: total 3.

explanationVariants: i² = −1, i⁴ = 1, i⁶ = −1 (remainder 2): the sum is −1 + 1 − 1 = −1.
Even powers alternate −1, 1, −1, … by remainder 2, 0, 2 — here that's −1.

widget.prompt: Compute i² + i⁴ + i⁶ as a real number.

commonErrors.feedback: The pattern is −1, +1, −1 — the odd-man-out is the +1 in the middle, and the sum is −1.
Not every even power is +1: remainder 2 gives −1, so it's −1 + 1 − 1 = −1.

hints: Reduce each exponent by its remainder when divided by 4.

steps.body: Powers of i cycle through i, −1, −i, 1 — every four steps.
takeaways: i¹ = i, i² = −1, i³ = −i, i⁴ = 1, then repeat.
For iⁿ, only the remainder of n ÷ 4 matters.
Remainder 0 means a whole number of laps: the value is 1.

concept.body: To find iⁿ, divide n by 4 and keep the remainder. i⁶: 6 = 4 + 2, remainder 2, so i⁶ = i².

options.feedback: 1 needs a multiple of 4 (i⁴ or i⁸) — 6 leaves remainder 2: −1.
